scope: Nearest-prior review for native regression exploration; not an exhaustive originality search

papers.title: Generalized Focal Loss: Learning Qualified and Distributed Bounding Boxes for Dense Object Detection
papers.reviewed: Sec3.2, equations4-6 and immediately following global minimum of DFL
papers.observation: The global minimum places linearly interpolated mass on the two adjacent target bins, recovers the continuous target exactly, and can have positive variance. Thus replacing the mean with integer mode/median is not inherently more accurate. Candidate37 subtracts the elementary integer-support variance floor as a testable hypothesis, not as a claimed new mathematical result.

papers.title: Generalized Focal Loss V2: Learning Reliable Localization Quality Estimation for Dense Object Detection
papers.observation: DFL distribution shape/statistics for localization quality are established prior art. Simple variance/entropy quality estimation cannot be claimed as innovation.

papers.title: D-FINE: Redefine Regression Task in DETRs as Fine-grained Distribution Refinement
papers.metadata_provenance: Search Service primary arXiv record and ICLR2025 proceedings; Paper Search Crossref query returned0 and is not evidence of absence
papers.reviewed: Sec4.1 equations2-4: residual refinement of edge distributions, weighted-sum decoding, nonuniform offset weighting and box-size scaling
papers.observation: Fine distribution refinement, nonuniform bins and size-scaled coordinate residuals already exist. A generic residual regression head or changing DFL decode is not itself an innovation.
